lyrics:
[Intro: warm electric guitar arpeggio, soft organ, slow swing]

[Verse 1: male tenor, tender, guitar and bass]
I had a dream the news came on
Said we had until the dawn
And I didn't pack a thing
I just drove to where you've been

[Chorus: both voices, full band, slow sway]
If the sky falls on a Tuesday
I'll be standing at your door
With nothing but a record
And the shoes I had before
We'll push the couch back to the wall
And dance until it's through
If the sky falls on a Tuesday
I'd spend it slow with you

[Verse 2: female voice, strong and warm, piano joins]
Let the sirens do their singing
Let the neighbours board the glass
I've been saving up a slow one
For a night I knew would pass

[Chorus: both voices, strings join]
If the sky falls on a Tuesday
I'll be standing at your door
With nothing but a record
And the shoes I had before
We'll push the couch back to the wall
And dance until it's through
If the sky falls on a Tuesday
I'd spend it slow with you

[Guitar Solo: bluesy, singing tone, over the chorus chords]

[Bridge: voices trading, building to a shared high note]
One more turn
(One more turn)
Hold me there
(Hold me there)
Let it fall

[Final Chorus: both at full power, harmonies, drums crashing]
If the sky falls on a Tuesday
I'll be standing at your door
With nothing but a record
And the shoes I had before
We'll push the couch back to the wall
And dance until it's through
If the sky falls on a Tuesday
I'd spend it slow with you

[Outro: guitar arpeggio, needle lifting off a record]
Slow, with you
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 79 BPM with a slow, swaying triplet swing, A major. A last-dance ballad that builds from a murmur to a roar.

VOICE: A male tenor with a sweet, soulful, slightly raspy tone and an easy falsetto. A female voice with great power and a theatrical edge, warm low down and blazing at the top. They take a verse each, sing the choruses in harmony, and reach a shared high note at the end of the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A warm, clean electric guitar playing arpeggios. Electric bass. A live drum kit with a slow, heavy backbeat. Piano. Hammond-style organ. A string section from the second chorus. A bluesy lead guitar solo. The sound of a record needle.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and organ. 0:12 Verse 1, the man. 0:36 Chorus 1, both voices and the band. 1:12 Verse 2, the woman. 1:36 Chorus 2, with strings. 2:12 Guitar solo. 2:30 Bridge, voices trading, rising to a shared high note. 2:48 Final chorus at full power. 3:24 Outro, the guitar arpeggio, a needle lifting from a record, three sung words at 3:42.

PRODUCTION & MIX: A 2020s recording made to sound like a mid-1970s soul-rock single: live band in a room, warm tape tone, voices big and slightly saturated.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first chorus, when the second voice joins and the drums come in at 0:36.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The end of the world arrives on an ordinary weekday, and the plan is a couch pushed back and an old record. It is devotion as people with a long shared history would spend it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Calm decision, tenderness, abandon, peace.
